cleanIntro: The Draco is a Romanian Cugir AK-pattern pistol imported by Century, and Century's own book covers the Draco, Mini Draco and Micro Draco together — each with its own specification block, identical mechanism, different barrel and overall length. Your row is the full-size Draco: a 12.25-inch barrel and 21.5 inches overall, the longest of the three. Two things drive this strip and neither is on the rifle version of the same action. The pistol has a RECOIL BUFFER behind the carrier that has to come out with the recoil spring assembly, and the whole spring assembly is under compression when you release it — Century's own note is to hold on to it or be hurt. And there is no magazine disconnect: with a round in the chamber this pistol fires with the magazine out, so the magazine leaves first and the chamber is checked second, always. The Draco field strip does NOT remove the gas cylinder tube, unlike Century's WASR rifle book — do not carry that step across.

steps.title: Safety lever fully up to SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction. Put the safety lever fully up to SAFE, then press the magazine release lever FORWARD — it is a lever ahead of the trigger guard, not a side button — and rock the magazine out of the receiver. Lay the magazine aside; it must be out of the pistol for everything that follows.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release lever forward to remove the magazine from the pistol.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Unloading the Pistol — p.9
steps.warn: WARNING! The pistol will fire if the magazine is removed and if the trigger is pulled when a cartridge is in the chamber.

steps.title: Safety to FIRE, bolt back, inspect the chamber, then SAFE again
steps.action: With the magazine out, move the safety lever down to FIRE — the AK safety physically blocks the charging handle in its up position, so the bolt cannot be retracted until it is lowered. Pull the bolt cocking handle back, look into the chamber and confirm it is empty, then let the bolt go forward and put the safety back up to SAFE. That order — magazine, then safety down, then look, then safety up — is Century's and it is the safe one.
steps.caution: WARNING! If dropped, any firearm could fire when there is a cartridge in the chamber and the safety lever is in the "FIRE" position.
steps.quote: 3. Move the safety lever to the “FIRE” position. (See Illustration #3.) Check the pistol's chamber to ensure it does not contain a round by pulling back on the bolt cocking handle. (See Illustration #4.) Inspect the chamber to ensure it is empty. Once you determine the chamber is empty and no magazine is in the pistol, let the bolt go forward. Move the safety lever to the "SAFE" position. (See Illustration #2.)
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Unloading the Pistol — p.9

steps.title: If a case will not extract, do not force it
steps.action: If a cartridge stays in the chamber after the trigger has been pulled and the extractor will not pull it out, take the magazine out and work the cocking handle several times. If that fails, RIDE the handle home slowly so the bolt never slams the case head, put the safety up to SAFE, and field strip the pistol before going any further. If it is still stuck after the strip, do not reassemble it — it goes to a gunsmith.
steps.quote: If after field stripping your pistol you are still unable to remove the cartridge casing, do not reassemble the pistol.Take the pistol to a competent gunsmith to remove the round and ensure proper functioning.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Unloading the Pistol — p.9

steps.title: Eye protection on, magazine confirmed out
steps.action: Shooting glasses or goggles on before anything moves. Century names spring tension as the reason, and this strip releases a compressed recoil spring assembly two steps from now. Confirm once more that the magazine is out and the chamber is empty.
steps.quote: WARNING! Wear eye protection, such as shooting glasses or goggles, when disassembling your firearm to protect your eyes from tensioned parts, such as springs that could be dislodged during disassembly.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Field Stripping — p.9
steps.warn: WARNING! Before beginning the disassembly process, check to ensure the pistol is not loaded. To do so, follow the procedures detailed in the Unloading the Pistol section on page 9.

steps.title: Recoil spring cam forward, receiver cover off REAR-FIRST
steps.action: Rest the pistol across your lap or on the table so it cannot move, grasp the rear of the receiver, and press the recoil spring cam forward. With the cam held forward the cover is unlatched — lift it away from the BACK end first. The front of the cover sits in a groove at the gas tube block and will not come out any other way.
steps.quote: 4. While maintaining a safe muzzle direction, remove the receiver cover by holding the pistol in a secure position (across your lap, resting on a table, etc.) and grasping the rear part of the receiver with your right hand, press the recoil spring cam forward. Then remove the receiver cover from the back end first. (See Illustration #10.)
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Field Stripping — p.10

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly and the recoil BUFFER out
steps.action: Grip the handguard, press the back of the recoil spring cam with your thumb into the notch cut in the back of the recoil buffer, lift the back of the cam clear of the buffer and pull the recoil spring assembly out of the bolt carrier channel. Then lift the recoil buffer itself out of the receiver and set it aside. Keep hold of the spring assembly the whole time — it is compressed and Century warns in the same breath that letting go can injure you.
steps.prose: The recoil buffer is a Draco-pattern part; the rifle version of this action does not have one and Century's WASR book never mentions it. Note which way round it sits — the notch faces the rear.
steps.quote: 5. While gripping the handguard in your hand, press the back of the recoil spring cam with your thumb into the notch cut into the back of the recoil buffer. (See Illustration #11.) Lift the back of the recoil spring cam until its clear of the buffer and pull the recoil spring assembly from the bolt carrier channel. Pull the recoil buffer out of the receiver and set it aside.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Field Stripping — p.10
steps.warn: NOTE:The recoil spring assembly is under spring pressure. Hold on to the assembly when removing it or injury could result.

steps.title: Bolt carrier and bolt back until they clear, then lift out
steps.action: Hold the receiver in one hand and the cocking handle in the other and pull the carrier and bolt rearward as far as they will go, until the back of the carrier meets the receiver's backplate. At that point — and only at that point — lift the rear of the carrier and take it and the bolt out of the receiver together.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the bolt carrier and bolt from the pistol by holding the receiver with your hand the cocking handle with your other hand. Pull the bolt carrier and bolt to the rear as far as possible. Once the back of the bolt carrier contacts the backplate of the receiver. Lift the rear portion of the bolt carrier and remove it and the bolt from the receiver. (See Illustration #12.)
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Field Stripping — p.10

steps.title: Bolt rotated right and out of the carrier — field strip complete
steps.action: Turn the carrier over in your hand. Rotate what is now the top of the bolt to the RIGHT and move it rearward so its guide lug leaves the channel in the carrier, then draw the bolt forward and out of its guide hole. That is the pistol stripped: receiver cover, recoil spring assembly, recoil buffer, bolt carrier and bolt. Century's book takes it no further and neither should you — the gas tube stays on this pistol, and the trigger group is not a user item.
steps.quote: 7. Remove the bolt from the bolt carrier by turning the bolt carrier over and holding it in your hand. (See Illustration #13.) Rotate what is now the top of the bolt to the right and move it rearward with your other hand so that the guide lug on the bolt leaves the channel in the bolt carrier.You can now remove the bolt from the bolt carrier by moving it forward and out of its guide hole.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Field Stripping — p.10

steps.title: Bore: 7.62 brush and solvent to a clean patch, then light oil
steps.action: Fit the correct-calibre brush to a rod, dampen it with solvent and push it through the barrel several times, then follow with correctly sized patches to carry the fouling out. Alternate until a patch comes out clean, then oil the bore lightly. A short AK pistol barrel fouls fast because so little of the powder has burned by the time the bullet leaves it.
steps.quote:
3. To clean the barrel, select the correct caliber cleaning brush and attach it to a cleaning rod. 4. Dampen the brush with gun cleaning solvent and then push the brush through the barrel
several times. 5. Remove the brush and attach a correctly sized cloth cleaning patch to the cleaning rod and
push it through the barrel several times to remove loosened fouling. 6. Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean
after swabbing the bore. Lightly oil the bore.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Cleaning the Pistol — p.12

steps.title: Action parts and outer surfaces: solvent, then take the solvent back off
steps.action: Wipe the action parts and the outside of the pistol with a soft cloth dabbed in solvent — bolt face, lug recesses, carrier rails, the piston head and the inside of the receiver. Then remove ALL the excess solvent and dry them; solvent left standing under oil is what pits an AK's thin receiver. Finish with a soft cloth dipped in good gun oil over the outer surfaces.
steps.caution: WARNING! There may be sharp edges on parts of the firearm. Keep your fingers protected by wearing a pair of protective gloves when cleaning.
steps.quote:
7. Remove shooting residue from the pistol's action parts and outer surfaces by wiping them
with a soft cloth dabbed in gun cleaning solvent. Then be sure to remove all excess solvent and dry them. 8. Finally, wipe down all outer surfaces with a soft cloth dipped in a good quality gun oil.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Cleaning the Pistol — p.12

steps.title: Do not over-solvent or over-oil it
steps.action: Century is explicit that too much solvent or lubricant will hurt how this pistol runs. Wipe the inside of the barrel DRY before firing and confirm it is free of obstructions. A short-barrelled AK pistol running wet with oil collects carbon into a paste faster than anything else in the catalogue.
steps.quote: WARNING! Excessive use of cleaning solvents or lubricants can adversely affect your pistol's functioning.Wipe the inside of the barrel dry before firing and ensure that it is free of obstructions.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Cleaning the Pistol — p.12

steps.title: Cleaning interval by climate, and the cold-weather lubricant
steps.action: Clean it as soon as you can after firing. Unfired, Century wants a full clean once or twice a year in a dry climate and up to weekly in a humid one. Below freezing, use a dry lubricant rather than oil — oil thickens and an AK pistol's short stroke has less margin to overcome it.
steps.aside: NOTE: In freezing weather (below 32° F. or 0° C.), the use of a dry lubricant (instead of oil) for lubrication may work better.
steps.quote: Always clean your pistol as soon as possible after firing to prevent buildup of shooting residue and to prevent corrosion from starting.To maintain your pistol in good working order, it should be cleaned regularly even if it has not been fired. If you live in a low-humidity area, this may mean doing a full clean once or twice a year; but if you live in a high-humidity area, it may be necessary to clean your pistol as often as once a week.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — DRACO SEMI-AUTO PISTOL — Cal. 7.62X39MM — Draco / Mini Draco / Micro Draco — March 2018 ("© March 2018 Century Arms" printed on page 1 and in every page footer) — Cleaning Intervals — p.12

deepAbsentReason: Century's Draco book stops at the field strip. Beyond the bolt-out-of-carrier step it publishes only reassembly, cleaning, cleaning intervals and storage, and it directs periodic inspection for worn or damaged parts to a competent gunsmith rather than to the owner. No trigger-group, gas-system or front-end teardown is documented anywhere in the 16 pages, so there is no deeper published procedure to walk.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Correct-calibre brush dampened with solvent, pushed through several times.
Correctly sized patches through to carry the loosened fouling out.
Alternate until a patch comes out clean, then oil the bore lightly.
Wipe the bore DRY again before firing and confirm it is free of obstructions.

cleaning.name: Bolt, carrier and buffer
tasks: Bolt face and lug recesses brushed with solvent.
Carrier rails, cam track and the gas piston head cleaned.
Recoil buffer wiped clean and inspected — it takes the beating on a short-barrelled pistol.
Recoil spring assembly wiped down; do not stretch the spring.

cleaning.name: Receiver and exterior
tasks: Action parts and outer surfaces wiped with solvent, then ALL excess solvent removed and dried.
Outer surfaces wiped with a soft cloth dipped in good quality gun oil.
Gloves on: stamped receiver edges are sharp.
Below freezing, dry lubricant instead of oil.

cleaning.name: Interval and inspection
tasks: After every firing session, as soon as possible.
Low-humidity climate: a full clean once or twice a year even unfired.
High-humidity climate: as often as weekly.
Periodic check for worn or damaged parts by a competent gunsmith.

reassembly: Bolt into carrier: carrier upside down, gas piston facing away, bolt face away and guide lug UP; insert the bolt shaft into the guide hole, bring it fully rearward, align the guide lug with the channel and rotate the bolt to the LEFT until it moves forward as far as it will go.
Confirm the hammer is COCKED — locked under the sear — before the carrier goes in. This is a named prerequisite, not a suggestion.
Carrier and bolt onto the receiver with a thumb on the back of the bolt holding it fully forward; align the back face of the carrier with the inside face of the receiver's backplate.
Depress the carrier against hammer-spring pressure with the heel of the hand so the carrier's side guide grooves line up with the receiver rails, then run it fully forward.
Recoil buffer back into the receiver with the NOTCH FACING THE REAR.

Recoil spring retainer into the bolt carrier channel; move the recoil spring cam forward over the notch in the buffer and press down until the guide lugs align with the channel in the receiver's rear block, then release so it moves rearward and locks.
Receiver cover: front edge into the groove at the back of the gas tube block, then press the back end forward and downward until the cam button locks it.
Safety lever back up to SAFE.
fncheck: With the pistol proven empty, magazine out and muzzle safe: press down on the receiver cover and confirm the cam button is holding it — a cover that lifts has not latched. Cycle the cocking handle several times and confirm the carrier travels fully rearward to the backplate and returns fully forward under spring pressure. Rotate the safety fully up and confirm the trigger will not move AND that the cocking handle is blocked; rotate it down and confirm both free up. Confirm the recoil buffer is seated notch-rearward by checking the cam sits in it. Last, wipe the bore dry and confirm it is clear before any ammunition is brought near the pistol.
